reports.category: Pig Butchering Scams: Learn and Report on Chainabuse
reports.description:
Coerced to depositing amounts into coinuped.com with unrealistic high returns generated and then unable to withdraw my money.
His name was Ezio. Met him on a social media platform before he suggested we talk on WhatsApp. He asked what I do and he said he’s into gold trading and crypto trading. I mentioned about how I had a small amount invested in stocks and crypto and he suggested he could help increase my returns given I haven’t been very successful with making money from investing in cryptocurrencies. He asked me to create an account on coinuped.com which is what he called a node trading platform (two node trading). Once I did he would give me the actual trades to conduct on the platform and the returns were very high. Kept encouraging me to deposit more to keep up with the market. At some point and to prove the platform was genuine he said he would show me how to withdraw funds from the platform and I did manage to withdraw like $400 just to demonstrate that it’s working. That obviously gave me some reassurance. At some point he suggested to take advantage of a gift activity where the platform would give you 10K of USDT if you deposit $100K within a week. He said I could with withdraw as soon as I complete the activity. Problems started after this when I tried to withdraw. Every time they would come up with a reason to deny the withdrawals saying the audit failed for some made up reason and I would have to deposit a % of my balance within a specified period of time otherwise I would lose my funds. Rather than stopping to think how this doesn’t make sense you’re occupied thinking about how you could make up the penalty amount so as not to lose the rest of your funds. A couple of times this happened and then I realized what I realized and by then it was too late. These guys are very good at what they do.

reports.category: Pig Butchering Scams: Learn and Report on Chainabuse
reports.description: I was targeted in a cryptocurrency romance scam. The scammer initially contacted me through an online dating app and soon convinced me to continue chatting on a private messaging app called LINE.After a few days of casual conversations about life and work, the scammer mentioned making good profits from cryptocurrency investments. As our conversations became more flirtatious, she offered to teach me how to invest in crypto.She guided me to download Binance and then directed me to download a separate “investment app,” claiming it was a crypto mining or staking platform. The website appeared secure with an “https://” link, which made me believe it was legitimate.To gain my trust, she had me invest a small amount first, walked me through the process, and even allowed me to successfully withdraw small profits. This led me to believe the platform was real.Soon after, she encouraged me to invest a larger amount, suggesting that I transfer AUD 15,000 (around 10,000 USDT) to a wallet address provided by the fake platform's customer support. She said this would help me earn higher returns quickly, claiming that she had invested heavily herself and encouraging me by saying “we are a couple now, we should earn together.”Due to bank restrictions on crypto transfers in Australia at the time, some of my attempts to send funds failed. The scammer then claimed to trust me so much that she deposited over 20,000 USDT from her own account into the platform on my behalf to keep things moving.When I later tried to withdraw the funds, the fake customer service claimed that my account had been flagged for “money laundering review” by an international regulator. They demanded that I deposit 50% of my total account balance as a “security deposit” to unfreeze the funds.As the deadline approached and I couldn't gather enough funds (though I had already sent part of it), the scammer claimed her own account had been locked because she tried transferring funds to a “flagged account” — meaning mine.The platform then threatened that a “government agency” would launch an investigation against me unless I paid the full amount immediately. At this point, I realized it was a scam, as no legitimate platform or government agency would require payments in this manner.
